D015-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling… off… for over a year now. Mostly, it’s this heaviness, like I’m stuck in slow motion. Nothing really interests me anymore—not books, not music, not even organizing the archives, which used to calm me. I just go through the motions. I forget things too—where I put files, appointments, even my keys. I tell myself it's just stress, but deep down, I wonder if I’m losing my mind.

There are times when I hear someone say something casual, like a comment on the weather, and I’m convinced they’re really talking about me—some kind of hidden message. I know it sounds odd, but it feels real in the moment. And sometimes, late at night, I feel something crawling on my arms, like insects, but when I look, there’s nothing there. I’ve checked the bedsheets, the windows—nothing. It stops when I focus on breathing, but it comes back.

I’ve had thoughts—dark ones. “I’d be better off dead,” that sort of thing. Not seriously, not with a plan, just… a quiet wish. I push through work because I have to, but some days, I don’t see the point. I can’t tell if the thoughts and sensations are from the sadness… or if the sadness is just following something else, something older.
D015-D005_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h001.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h002.question:
Lately, it’s been hard to even get out of bed. I’ve felt this heavy sadness for over a year now—like nothing matters anymore. I used to love doing nails, picking colors for clients, chatting with them… now, I don’t feel anything when I do it. Doesn’t bring me joy, not even a little. I can’t decide simple things—like what to eat or what to wear—even picking a nail polish feels impossible. I just stand there, frozen.  

Sometimes, I catch this strange smell—like something’s rotting—no one else does, but it’s strong to me. I’ve started worrying something inside me is decayed, maybe in my stomach or chest. Doctors checked, said everything’s fine, but I can’t shake the feeling.  

Most days, I think… I wish I wouldn’t wake up. Not that I’d do anything, just—what’s the point?  

The smells and thoughts about my body… I know they sound strange, but they feel real. I don’t know if it’s stress from work, or something deeper. I used to be able to push through, but not anymore. I can’t tell if the dark mood comes first… or the smells and thoughts. It’s all tangled.
D015-D005_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h002.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been feeling empty for over a year now—like there’s just nothing inside. Some days, I don’t even know if I want to wake up. I used to worry about things, care about my routines, but it’s all just… foggy now. Thinking feels like wading through sludge. I’ve stopped calling friends, even my sister. What’s the point? I’m stuck maintaining these old COBOL systems at work—same code for decades. Feels like I’m just preserving something long dead.

Lately, I’ve seen things. Shadows in the hallway, figures standing at the foot of the bed. They don’t move. Don’t speak. But I *see* them. And sometimes I’m sure the world… isn’t real anymore. Like everything’s already ended—just no one turned the lights off. The city, the job, people walking by—it all feels like a simulation running on a dead machine.

I don’t know if it’s the grief—my wife’s been gone four years—or if something’s breaking in my head. The sadness came first, but these thoughts… these visions… they don’t feel tied to it. Or maybe they do. I can’t tell anymore.
D015-D005_h003.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h003.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been feeling this heavy sadness for over a year now—like a constant weight. Nothing gives me joy anymore, not even seeing my clients close a deal or spending time with my husband. It’s hard to get dressed in the morning, and even picking what to eat feels overwhelming. I’ll stand in front of the closet for 20 minutes, paralyzed, like I’m afraid I’ll make the wrong choice.  

Sometimes I hear my name whispered when no one’s around—soft, familiar voices saying things like, “You’re special,” or “They love you more than you know.” I keep thinking my old college professor, who I haven’t seen in years, watches me, not in a scary way, but like he’s waiting for me to notice. He’s trying to save me, I think? Or maybe tell me something important.  

The worst part is these sudden urges—when I’m on a high floor showing an apartment, I’ll get this intense pull to step over the balcony. No plan, just this impulse, like a flash. I pull back, scared, but it keeps happening.  

I don’t know if this is because I’m depressed or if I’m losing touch with reality. The voices were here before the sadness, I think? Or was it the other way around? I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D015-D005_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h004.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling… empty for over a year now. It started slowly—just not getting joy from things I used to love, like planning content or even scrolling through the feeds I used to find so fun. Now it’s like I’m watching my life through a foggy window. I can’t feel anything, not excitement, not sadness—just numb. I forget things constantly—where I put my keys, if I even locked the door. My team has noticed I miss deadlines, and honestly, some days I just don’t care. 

And then there are the thoughts—dark ones. Not all the time, but often enough: *I wish I wasn’t here*, *I wouldn’t mind if I just didn’t wake up*. I don’t have a plan or anything, but they don’t go away.

About six months in, things got… weird. I started seeing shadows in my apartment—figures standing in the corners, especially at night. I know they’re not real, but they feel so solid. Sometimes I wonder if my landlord has cameras or if people online are tracking me through my phone. I can’t prove it, but it feels like someone’s always watching. I don’t know what’s worse—the emptiness or the things I keep seeing.
D015-D005_h005.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Anorexia Nervosa
D015-D005_h005.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h006.question: I’ve felt completely hollow for the past four months—like there’s nothing inside, not even sadness. I wake up and it’s as if I’m already done with the day. I keep going over things I said in rehearsals, lines I flubbed years ago, things people probably don’t even remember. I punished myself over them then, and now it’s constant. I took a bottle of pills back in February—just sat on the bathroom floor and swallowed them. My husband found me. I don’t want to die, not really, but sometimes it feels like the world is already ending. Not in a loud way—just... emptying out, like everything’s fading to gray and won’t come back. I lie in bed at night and feel something crawling on my arms, like insects under the sheets, but when I turn on the light, there’s nothing. No one’s touched me. I stopped wearing long sleeves because the fabric makes it worse. I can’t perform. I was supposed to open in a new show last month, but I couldn’t remember my blocking, my voice kept breaking. It’s not just the depression—sometimes I wonder if I’m feeling the truth no one else can, or if my mind’s breaking for good.
D015-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h006.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been… gone, for about four months now. Just going through the motions at the shop, chopping and wrapping meat like a machine. My wife passed two years ago, but lately it feels like something heavier settled in. I can’t feel anything—no sadness, no anger, nothing. It’s like my soul’s been numbed. 

Lately, I keep seeing her—clear as day—in the back room of the butcher shop. She doesn’t speak, just watches. And not just her… sometimes figures in white coats standing near the freezers, though no one else sees them. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I’m sure I’ve done something terrible. I didn’t just lose her—I *killed* her. I must’ve. Why else would God make me survive and not her? I keep thinking about using the band saw. I’ve pictured it: after closing, when it’s just me and the lights overhead. I’d know how—it’s sharp, fast. No one would hear over the exhaust fan.

People say I’ve changed. I used to be proud of my cuts, but now I can’t focus. Orders get wrong. But part of me also thinks… maybe I’m meant for more. I’ve had moments—rare ones—where I feel like I’m not just a butcher. Like I have a message, something divine. But then the guilt comes crashing back. I don’t know what’s real anymore.
D015-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h007.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been feeling heavy for about four months now—like I’m moving through water every day. I can’t seem to shake this deep sadness, no matter what I do. Some mornings, I don’t even want to get out of bed. Work has suffered. I used to be on top of my accounts, chasing leads, closing deals—but now I miss deadlines, forget calls. I catch myself thinking, *I’d be better off dead*, but I wouldn’t actually do anything—I just don’t see a way out sometimes.

The weirdest part is the voices. Not all the time, but at night, I hear someone whispering my name from the other room. Once, I heard a man say I was “chosen,” like I had some kind of special purpose. It sounds crazy, but it felt real. Sometimes I wonder if I’m more important than people realize—like there’s a reason I’m hearing these things. But other days, I doubt it all. I can’t tell what’s real anymore.
D015-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h008.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h009.question: I’ve just been crying all the time—at open houses, in my car between showings, even in front of clients. It’s so embarrassing, but I can’t stop. For four months now, it’s like a fog I can’t shake. I keep thinking I’ve ruined everything—my marriage, my work. I’ll hear my husband talking to someone on the phone, and I just *know* he’s arranging to meet someone else, even when there’s no real reason to think that. I can’t help it. And sometimes, I smell something burning—like plastic or hair—it’s sharp, it hits me fast, but no one else ever notices. It’s probably nothing. But these thoughts… I wish I wouldn’t wake up some mornings. I don’t want to act on it—no plan or anything—but the idea feels like a relief. I keep thinking maybe I’ve done something so wrong that this is my punishment. Maybe I’ve pushed everyone away on purpose because I don’t feel like I deserve them. I don’t know what’s real anymore—those smells, the fear about my husband—but it all feels true when it’s happening.
D015-D005_h009.options:

    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D015-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling… hollow for about four months now. It’s like I’m watching life through a fogged-up window. I used to care so deeply—my clients, my friends, even little things like watering my plants—but now nothing moves me. I just go through the motions. I can’t stop thinking that I’ve failed people. Last week, I spilled coffee at work and spent the whole day convinced I’d ruined someone’s paperwork, maybe even a child’s case file. I kept thinking I deserved to be fired—or worse. I don’t know why it hit me that way. Sometimes I whisper, “I just want to disappear,” but I won’t act on it. I’m not planning anything.

For the past few weeks—maybe longer—I’ve seen shadows moving in the corners of my apartment, figures that vanish when I turn. Once, I saw a man standing in the hallway who wasn’t there. And I’m convinced something’s wrong with my heart. It doesn’t feel normal—like it’s shrinking or rotting, though the doctor found nothing. I can’t say how long the voices or images have been there without the sadness, or if they’ll stay after. Some days I can’t tell what’s real.
D015-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D015-D005_h010.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling really off for about seven months now. Some days, I just start crying for no reason—like, I’ll be working on a design and suddenly I can’t see the screen through tears. I don’t know why it happens. Sleep doesn’t help much either. I get eight hours, sometimes more, but I wake up exhausted, like my brain’s been running all night. Focusing on layouts or even replying to emails takes so much effort. I’ll stare at the screen and my thoughts just… stall.

And then there are these thoughts—like I’m being watched. Not in a scary movie way, but it feels real. I swear my landlord has cameras in the vents, or that my boss is tracking my phone. I know it sounds strange, but the way people look at me, the timing of random things… it can’t all be coincidence. Sometimes I wonder if it’s just because I’m so drained all the time, but even when I’m not feeling sad, that feeling lingers. I can’t tell if it’s part of the depression or something else entirely. I just know I can’t work like this anymore.
D015-D005_h011.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D015-D005_h011.answer: C & A. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features & Schizophrenia

D015-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about seven months now. Work used to be manageable—leading audit teams, coordinating deadlines—but now I can’t focus. My brain feels heavy, like I’m pushing through fog just to read an email. I’m exhausted all the time, even though I sleep ten, sometimes twelve hours a night—and still nap in the afternoon. My wife complains I’m always in bed, but I can’t help it. I don’t find joy in anything anymore, not even my kid’s soccer games.

And then there’s this… belief. I know it sounds strange, but I’m convinced something’s wrong internally—my organs are rotting, somehow. Doctors ran tests, said everything’s fine, but I *feel* it. It’s not like I see it or hear it—I just *know* it’s happening. It’s constant. I’ve tried working through it, but my performance’s slipped. Missed details, delayed reports. My boss noticed.

I can’t tell if this started with the sadness or came later. The lines are blurred. Some days I wonder if I’m losing my mind—but not in the way people think. It’s quieter. Just me, the fatigue, and this body betrayal I can’t shake.

A. Schizophrenia

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h013.question:

A. Schizophrenia

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h014.question:

A. Schizophrenia
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D015-D005_h015.question:

D015-D005_h016.question:

D015-D005_h017.question:

A. Schizophrenia

    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

D015-D005_h019.question:

D015-D005_h020.question:

D015-D005_h021.question:

A. Schizophrenia
